description: Builds a real wg-quick tunnel (tctest0) to a WireGuard peer in its own network namespace, then proves: bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is touched; a stopped tunnel that is not enabled is left down (NOT_ACTIVE); once enabled it is started and a handshake is confirmed (RESTARTED); a healthy tunnel is left alone; with the peer down a restart reports STILL_UNHEALTHY; a second run inside the cooldown does nothing; Always restarts regardless; a WireGuard interface not managed by wg-quick, one with no peers, a non-WireGuard interface and a config that does not parse are reported and not touched.

steps.label: Refuses an empty interface
Refuses an interface name with shell characters
Refuses an unknown mode
Refuses a handshake age under 150
Refuses a verify time over 120
Refuses a ping target that looks like an option
Install wireguard-tools; build tctest0's config and a peer in namespace tcpeer
steps.run:
set -e
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
apt-get update -qq >/dev/null && apt-get install -y -qq wireguard-tools >/dev/null
modprobe wireguard
umask 077; mkdir -p /etc/wireguard /root/tcwg
for k in a b; do wg genkey > /root/tcwg/$k.key; wg pubkey < /root/tcwg/$k.key > /root/tcwg/$k.pub; done
printf '[Interface]\nPrivateKey = %s\nAddress = 10.99.0.1/32\nListenPort = 51820\n\n[Peer]\nPublicKey = %s\nAllowedIPs = 10.99.0.2/32\nEndpoint = 127.0.0.1:51821\n' "$(cat /root/tcwg/a.key)" "$(cat /root/tcwg/b.pub)" > /etc/wireguard/tctest0.conf
ip netns add tcpeer
ip link add tcpeer0 type wireguard
wg set tcpeer0 private-key /root/tcwg/b.key listen-port 51821 peer "$(cat /root/tcwg/a.pub)" allowed-ips 10.99.0.1/32 endpoint 127.0.0.1:51820
ip link set tcpeer0 netns tcpeer
ip -n tcpeer addr add 10.99.0.2/32 dev tcpeer0
ip -n tcpeer link set tcpeer0 up
ip -n tcpeer route add 10.99.0.1/32 dev tcpeer0
echo setup-ok

steps.label: Tunnel down and not enabled: left down
Enable wg-quick@tctest0 without starting it
steps.run: systemctl enable wg-quick@tctest0 2>&1; systemctl is-active wg-quick@tctest0 || true

steps.label: Enabled but down: started, handshake confirmed
The tunnel carries traffic
steps.run: ping -c 2 -W 2 10.99.0.2 && wg show tctest0 latest-handshakes | awk '{print ($2 > 0) ? "handshaked" : "never"}'

steps.label: Healthy: left alone
Second run: still nothing to do
Take the peer down, and the interface administratively down
steps.run: ip -n tcpeer link set tcpeer0 down && ip link set tctest0 down && echo broken

steps.label: Unhealthy, peer unreachable: restarted, reported still unhealthy
Cooldown stamp written
Make it unhealthy again
steps.run: ip link set tctest0 down && echo down

steps.label: Inside the cooldown: not restarted again
Bring the peer back
steps.run: ip -n tcpeer link set tcpeer0 up && (ip -n tcpeer route add 10.99.0.1/32 dev tcpeer0 2>/dev/null || true) && echo peer-up

steps.label: Always, inside the cooldown: restarted anyway, handshake confirmed
Add a WireGuard interface by hand, outside wg-quick, with a peer that never answers
steps.run: ip link add tchand0 type wireguard && wg set tchand0 private-key /root/tcwg/a.key peer "$(cat /root/tcwg/b.pub)" allowed-ips 10.98.0.2/32 && ip link set tchand0 up && echo made

steps.label: Not managed by wg-quick: not touched
The hand-made interface is still there
steps.run: ip -o link show dev tchand0 >/dev/null && echo still-there

steps.label: Add a WireGuard interface with no peers
steps.run: ip link add tcempty0 type wireguard && ip link set tcempty0 up && echo made

steps.label: No peers: reported, not restarted
Not a WireGuard interface: refused
Break the config, then stop the tunnel
steps.run: systemctl stop wg-quick@tctest0 && echo 'NotAKey = 1' >> /etc/wireguard/tctest0.conf && echo broken

steps.label: Config does not parse: not started
Host without wireguard-tools reports NOT_INSTALLED
Internal gateway: stop the far end, wait past the threshold, run it; expect STILL_UNHEALTHY, and no restart loop under a monitor response
